title: RFID Plant Nursery Label — UV-Stable 12 mo Outdoor
summary: RFID plant nursery labels are passive UHF tags that survive 12+ months of full-sun UV, irrigation and soil on 1-25 gallon pots. UV-stabilised polypropylene and outdoor-rated acrylic adhesive resist fungicide, pesticide and fertiliser chemistry across -20 °C to +60 °C cycling. Each label carries the GS1 SGTIN-96 EPC plus USDA APHIS PPQ and state Nursery Stock Certificate IDs, and a pallet portal builds the EDI 856 ASN for big-box retailers in under 15 minutes.
heroPoints: UV-stabilised polypropylene + outdoor-rated acrylic adhesive — full-sun UV, overhead irrigation, soil splash, fertiliser / fungicide / pesticide chemistry; 12+ months outdoor service life.

Pre-encoded EPC + variety + pot size + APHIS PPQ certificate number + state Nursery Stock Certificate ID; supports EU Plant Passport 2016/2031 + Commission Reg 2017/2313 format via GS1 Digital Link URI.
Pallet RFID portal builds the EDI 856 Advance Ship Notice + GS1-128 SSCC label automatically — 1,000 pots in <15 min vs 4-6 h manual barcode capture for big-box retailer compliance.

brief.label: Substrate stack — UV, soil and chemical exposure
items: Top face — UV-stabilised polypropylene 100 µm with HALS (hindered amine light stabiliser) + UV absorber package; ASTM G154 cycle 1 ≥1,000 hours QUV-A.
Inlay — passive UHF EPC Gen2v2 chip on Al-etched PET antenna with conformal moisture coat.
Adhesive — outdoor-rated permanent acrylic, peel ≥18 N/25 mm to PE / PP / HDPE pots; weatherometer 12+ months at +60 °C / 95% RH.
Release liner — silicone-coated PET; thermal-transfer / digital-UV print compatible.

brief.label: Form factor variants
items: Pot-stake label — 25×80 mm rigid spike inserted in container substrate, visible on top of pot.
Pot-wrap label — 30×100 mm flexible adhesive wrap on outside of pot; survives daily irrigation.
Plug-tray label — 12×40 mm thin label on each cell of 50 / 72 / 128-cell plug trays.
Flat-tag label — 40×100 mm label on the rim of nursery flats; one tag per flat for plug-stage tracking.
B&B (balled-and-burlapped) tag — 50×120 mm UV-stable polyolefin loop tag on burlap stem; tolerates field UV + irrigation.

brief.label: Chip silicon and read distance
items: {chip:impinj-m730:name} — read sensitivity -22.7 dBm, default for nursery + retail mix.
{chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:name} — proven >5-year outdoor reliability, retail-source compatible.
{chip:nxp-ucode-8:name} — robust + cost-effective for high-volume pot-stake.
{chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} — highest UCODE-family sensitivity, suited for dense block reads.
Handheld 1.5-3 m on 3-gal pot; portal 4-6 m on pallet of 1-gal pots; line-speed reader 8-12 m/min on conveyor.

brief.label: Encoding — what goes on every label
items: GS1 SGTIN-96 EPC — GTIN-14 + serial number; serves as pot-level Item Identifier.
User memory — variety code (botanical binomial), pot size (1-25 gal), production date, growing zone / block ID, crop-stage, wholesale price tier.
USDA APHIS PPQ phytosanitary certificate number + state Nursery Stock Certificate ID encoded into a state-specific TID block.
GS1 Digital Link 1.3 URI ('https://nursery.com/01/<gtin>/21/<serial>') resolves to PHIS / EU Plant Passport / consumer-tap PDP per jurisdiction.
Lock bits + AFI byte armed per customer specification.

brief.label: What this product is NOT
items: Not a chip-level frozen-food label — adhesive Tg unsuited for blast-freezer (-40 °C); use the dedicated frozen-food label.
Not a HF NFC consumer-tap label — UHF for inventory + portal reads; pair with NTAG21x consumer-tap label on retail-ready stake if needed.
Not a plant-health sensor — pair with pH / EC / soil-moisture sensors at the block level.
Not a substitute for the printed plant tag — most nurseries keep the printed tag for visual species identification + retail consumer.

sections.title: USDA APHIS + EU 2016/2031 + ISPM 15 — the regulatory architecture this label is designed for

dataHighlight.heading: EU Plant Health Regulation 2016/2031 in force — Plant Passport mandatory for intra-EU movement of listed plants
dataHighlight.text: EU Reg 2016/2031 replaced Directive 2000/29/EC and established a risk-based Union quarantine pest list (Reg (EU) 2019/2072), with Plant Passport mandatory for intra-EU movement of listed plants (operator registration number, botanical binomial, traceability code, country of origin). Commission Implementing Reg (EU) 2017/2313 specifies the plant passport format; many EU authorised operators encode the passport data as a GS1 Digital Link URI ('https://nursery.com/01/<gtin>/21/<serial>') resolvable to the full certificate at customs scan. On the US side, USDA APHIS PPQ regulates interstate (7 CFR 301) and international (7 CFR 319) movement of nursery stock with phytosanitary certificates referenced per shipment-level identifier; ISPM 15 (FAO 2002 revised 2018) governs wood packaging across borders with HT or MB treatment marking. The RFID nursery label EPC associates the pot with all three trails — APHIS PPQ phytosanitary cert, state Nursery Stock Cert, and EU Plant Passport — so a single handheld scan at receiving captures the full compliance lineage.

faq.question: Will the label survive outdoor nursery conditions for a full growing season?
faq.answer: Yes. UV-stabilised polypropylene face stock with HALS + UV-absorber package on outdoor-rated permanent acrylic adhesive (peel ≥18 N/25 mm to PE/PP/HDPE), tested to ASTM G154 cycle 1 ≥1,000 hours QUV-A and weatherometer 12+ months at +60 °C / 95% RH. Real-world service life covers full-sun exposure, daily overhead irrigation, soil splash, fertiliser / fungicide / pesticide chemistry and -20 °C to +60 °C cycling. Printed text and RFID performance remain intact through the growing season; we supply COA on UV stability and adhesive-peel testing on request.

faq.question: Can the label be read when the pot is wet from irrigation?
faq.answer: Yes. UHF 13.56 MHz signals are minimally affected by surface water on the label face. Our nursery labels maintain reliable handheld reads at 1-3 m even when label and pot are dripping wet from overhead irrigation. Water pooling directly on the antenna reduces range by 10-20% but readings remain reliable at typical handheld scanning distances. For dense blocks where every pot is wet simultaneously, dock-door portal reads at 4-6 m on pallet build are the recommended workflow rather than handheld block sweeps during irrigation cycles.

faq.question: How does RFID improve wholesale order accuracy?
faq.answer: Each plant's RFID tag encodes the variety code + pot size + production date + crop-stage + wholesale price tier. During order picking, the handheld reader is loaded with the order details and guides the worker to the correct growing block and pot row. As each plant is picked, the reader confirms variety and size match the order line; mismatches trigger an immediate alert preventing wrong-variety and wrong-size errors before the order leaves the nursery. At pallet build, the RFID portal scan generates the EDI 856 Advance Ship Notice with GS1-128 SSCC pallet label automatically — 1,000 pots in <15 min vs 4-6 h manual barcode capture, and ASN-rejection fees from Home Depot / Lowe's / Walmart / Costco vendor-compliance failure are eliminated.

faq.question: How does RFID support USDA APHIS phytosanitary and state plant-quarantine compliance?
faq.answer: Each RFID EPC is unique per pot and is linked in the nursery ERP to the USDA APHIS PPQ phytosanitary certificate number, state Nursery Stock Certificate ID, inspection date, and origin greenhouse / field block. When a plant ships across state lines or internationally, the handheld scan captures the full compliance lineage without manual certificate matching. If a downstream pest detection (Phytophthora ramorum, citrus greening / HLB, boxwood blight, emerald ash borer, spotted lanternfly) triggers a recall or quarantine action, the EPC-linked records enable instant traceback to all affected shipments within minutes vs days of paper-record review. For EU-destined shipments under Plant Health Regulation 2016/2031, the same EPC encodes a GS1 Digital Link URI resolvable to the full plant passport data (operator registration number, botanical binomial, traceability code, country of origin) per Commission Implementing Reg 2017/2313.

faq.question: How does RFID integrate with nursery ERP and big-box retailer EDI shipping mandates?
faq.answer: Our RFID nursery labels integrate with leading horticultural ERP platforms — SBI Software Growing Assistant, Advanced Nursery Systems NurseryWorks, Practical Software Solutions MyPlantShop, Starcom Technologies NMS, Linnaeus CareManager — through standard REST API or CSV import of EPC-to-SKU mappings. At pallet build-time, a handheld scan of 500-1,000 pots captures every variety, size and order-line association, then generates the EDI 856 Advance Ship Notice with GS1-128 SSCC pallet labels automatically for Home Depot Vendor Compliance, Lowe's LowesLink, Walmart Retail Link and Costco Vendor Onboarding. This eliminates 4-6 h of manual barcode capture per pallet and the rejection fees associated with ASN inaccuracies. For cold-chain transit of tropicals and perennials, RFID pot labels pair with reusable temperature loggers (Sensitech TempTale, DeltaTrak FlashLink) at pallet level, providing dispute-resolution evidence if arrival quality issues occur after multi-day transcontinental truck moves.
